principle: Use the highest-authority source that directly supports the claim. Search results and secondary summaries are discovery aids, not automatic production truth.

sources.name: DailyMed Structured Product Labeling
sources.verification_notes: Prefer exact SPL setid/version/published date and section locator.

sources.name: Drugs@FDA
sources.verification_notes: Use for regulatory approval truth; do not infer approval from trial or company announcement.

sources.name: FDA Drug Development and Drug Interactions tables
sources.verification_notes: Tables are examples, not exhaustive lists. Preserve strength/classification and table context.

sources.name: FDA / ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies
sources.verification_notes: Use for general DDI interpretation methodology rather than patient-specific dose instructions.

sources.name: FDA Pharmacogenetic Associations / Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers
sources.verification_notes: Do not turn PK-only gene associations into efficacy/toxicity claims. Check drug label for management details.

sources.name: FDA Drug Safety Communications
sources.verification_notes: Track publication date and whether communication led to label changes.

sources.name: EMA EPAR / Summary of Product Characteristics
sources.verification_notes: Capture EPAR/product-information update date and jurisdiction.

sources.name: Center for Drug Evaluation, NMPA
sources.verification_notes: Preserve China jurisdiction and distinguish CDE review/acceptance from NMPA approval.

sources.name: National Health Commission of the PRC
sources.verification_notes: Check publication year/version; clinical pathways may be older and should not silently override newer specialty guidance.

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
sources.verification_notes: Registration proves trial metadata, not efficacy or causality.

sources.name: RxNorm / RxNav
sources.verification_notes: Use for identity/normalization, not as the clinical source of contraindication or dosing truth.

sources.name: LOINC
sources.verification_notes: Use to identify tests/observations; interpretation thresholds still require clinical sources.

sources.name: PubMed
sources.verification_notes: PubMed is an index; clinical claims must be verified against article design/results and preferably guideline/regulatory context.

sources.name: NIH LiverTox
sources.verification_notes: Use for DILI context; patient-specific management should still be anchored to current clinical guidance/label where applicable.

sources.name: openFDA / FAERS
sources.verification_notes: Never use a report count to establish causality or incidence; reporting is incomplete and biased.

sources.name: MedlinePlus Drug Information
sources.verification_notes: Useful for patient-facing task design; high-risk prescribing truth should be checked against approved/current labels and guidelines.

sources.name: WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines
sources.verification_notes: Global prioritization source; not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific labeling or individual treatment guidance.
